_README: K-pop-for-visitors guide (English base). EVERGREEN + fact-safe: concert venues, ticket platforms, weekly music shows, agency neighborhoods and fan landmarks. NO concert dates or tour schedules (those are volatile) — the `live` block links out to kpophub.kr + official ticketers instead. `spot` = frozen Google Maps query (keep English). `url` = frozen. Translated per locale in kpop.<locale>.json.

ui.metaTitle: K-pop in Korea: Concerts, Venues, Tickets & Fan Guide (2026)
ui.metaDesc: A K-pop fan's guide to Korea — concert venues, how to buy tickets, watching weekly music shows live, agency neighborhoods (HYBE, SM, JYP, YG) and fan landmarks. Current concert dates via kpophub.kr.
ui.tagline: A visiting fan's guide — venues, tickets, live music shows, agency spots and where to feel the scene.

live.title: Concerts & events happening now
live.body: Concert line-ups change all the time, so we don't freeze dates here — they'd just go stale. For current K-pop concerts, tours and events, check the live listings:
live.note: The official ticket platforms below also show what's on sale right now.

venues.title: Where the concerts happen
venues.intro: Most big K-pop concerts, tours and award shows land at a handful of large venues around Seoul and Incheon.

items.name: Inspire Arena
items.d: Korea's largest indoor arena, part of the Inspire resort right by Incheon Airport — a major stop for big concerts and award shows.

items.name: Gocheok Sky Dome
items.d: Korea's first domed stadium; its scale makes it a go-to for the biggest solo and group concerts.

items.name: KSPO Dome
items.d: A classic large indoor arena in Olympic Park (the Olympic Gymnastics Arena), long a home for major K-pop concerts.

items.name: Jamsil Sports Complex
items.d: The Jamsil stadium and indoor arena host stadium-scale tours and music festivals.

items.name: Olympic Hall
items.d: A mid-size hall used for showcases, fan meetings and smaller concerts.

tickets.title: How to get tickets
tickets.intro: K-pop tickets sell through a few official Korean platforms. Foreign fans can usually use the English 'Global' versions — but popular shows sell out in minutes, so prepare ahead.
steps: Make your account early on the ticketing site, and join the artist's fan club if there's a members' presale.
Note the exact on-sale time in Korea time (KST) and be logged in and ready a few minutes before.
Check payment and ID rules first — some sites need a card that works in Korea or a verified phone number.
If a show is sold out, only use official resale — never street scalpers.

platforms.name: Interpark Global
platforms.what: The biggest K-pop concert ticketer, with an English global site.

platforms.name: Yes24 Ticket
platforms.what: A major ticketer for concerts, fan meetings and musicals.

platforms.name: Melon Ticket
platforms.what: Ticketing tied to the Melon music service.

platforms.name: Weverse
platforms.what: Fan platform for HYBE and partner artists — some sales and fan-club perks run here.

musicShows.title: Watch a live music show
musicShows.intro: Korea's weekly TV music shows tape in front of a live audience, and many let fans in for free — a chance to see several artists perform in one afternoon.

shows.name: Music Bank (KBS)
shows.d: One of the longest-running weekly music shows.

shows.name: M Countdown (Mnet)
shows.d: Mnet's weekly show, known for elaborate stages.

shows.name: Show Champion (MBC M)
shows.d: A midweek show that is often easier to get into.

tips: Audience spots are usually organized through the performing artist's fan cafe or fan club — you apply in advance.
Some shows have limited standby spots on the day; expect an early start and a long wait.
Rules and schedules change often — always check the broadcaster's current guidance before you go.

agencies.title: Where the agencies are
agencies.intro: Fans often visit the 'Big 4' agency neighborhoods for the buildings and the cafes and shops around them. Buildings and rosters change over time, so treat this as orientation, not a live directory.

items.name: HYBE
items.d: HYBE's headquarters sits in central Yongsan — home to labels behind acts such as BTS and SEVENTEEN.

items.name: SM Entertainment
items.d: SM's headquarters is in the trendy Seongsu café district, where its KWANGYA@SEOUL flagship store sells official goods for acts such as aespa, NCT and RIIZE. It's a fan pilgrimage — pair it with a café crawl and the pop-up stores that fill the neighbourhood.

items.name: JYP Entertainment
items.d: JYP's building is in eastern Seoul — home to acts such as TWICE and Stray Kids.

items.name: YG Entertainment
items.d: YG sits in Hapjeong near Hongdae — home to acts such as BLACKPINK and TREASURE — easy to combine with a night out.

spots.title: K-pop fan landmarks
spots.intro: A few spots are made for fans to soak up the scene.

items.name: K-Star Road
items.d: A street lined with 'GangnamDol' art figures representing K-pop groups, in upscale Apgujeong-Cheongdam near many agencies and studios.

items.name: COEX & SMTOWN
items.d: The COEX complex has K-pop-themed spaces and the famous Starfield Library.

items.name: Hongdae busking street
items.d: Weekend evenings bring dance crews and singers performing K-pop covers around Hongik University.

items.name: Pop-up cafes & photo events
items.d: Seongsu is the epicentre: idols and groups run limited-time pop-up cafés and photo exhibitions in its converted-warehouse spaces (Hongdae and the big malls host them too). They move around, so check what's on when you visit — some need a timed reservation.
